findings.source: User screenshot M7-D2 and direct feedback, 2026-11-15
findings.observation: Entry to map: Piazza/Quaderno/Banco and generic exploration instruction do not explain purpose of each destination or next meaningful action; learner proceeds by trial and error.
findings.proposal: Brief character-led contextual mission reminder, explicit reason to investigate objects, visible contextual interaction cues, optional guidance and freedom of exploration; no long instruction wall.
findings.acceptance: A first-time learner can explain goal and choose a meaningful next action without external guidance; validate with teacher walkthrough before promotion.

findings.source: User screenshot M7-D2 and direct feedback, 2026-11-15
findings.observation: After selecting Piazza by trial, message 'Il lampione appare affievolito. L’immagine non è una misura: la causa rimane ignota.' is almost incomprehensible to user; abstract epistemic caveat replaces meaningful clue and offers no next action.
findings.proposal: Use short contextual character-led clue in age-appropriate language, explaining observation, mission and meaningful next step toward notebook/bench; retain scientific uncertainty in plain language, do not imply lamp replacement diagnoses or repairs fault.
findings.acceptance: First-time learner understands what was observed, what remains unknown and why the next action matters; teacher validates wording and scientific distinction. No implementation until findings collection ends.

findings.source: User screenshot M7-D2 and direct feedback, 2026-11-15
findings.observation: Message 'Nel modello virtuale, A trasferisce più energia termica di B.' introduces undefined A/B references and energy terminology before learner has met the models or understood the comparison. Information lacks a referent and purpose.
findings.proposal: Reorder conceptual progression: contextual observation about light and heat, question about energy use, introduce labelled virtual lamps at bench, compare under equal useful-light conditions, then name and explain efficiency. Notebook clue should be a comprehensible character observation/question, not an unexplained conclusion; preserve scientific uncertainty and model scope.
findings.acceptance: First-time learner can identify what each term and object refers to, explain why the clue matters, and connect it to the experiment without external explanation. Review all clues for prerequisite vocabulary, sequencing and cognitive load; no implementation until findings collection ends.

findings.source: User screenshot M7-D2 and direct feedback, 2026-11-15
findings.observation: User describes bench as hermetic, incomprehensible, without story or involvement, emotionally cold despite warm colors. Identical-looking lamps, undefined 20 J and energy indicators, prediction buttons and station do not communicate meaningful action or reason for it; characters absent from the interaction.
findings.proposal: Rebuild scene around character-led shared inquiry, contextual action cues, an optional guided initial demonstration or prediction based on comprehensible evidence, progressive introduction of model terms and controls, and visible consequences of actions. Preserve open exploration, scientific model, accessible alternatives, and avoid revealing the entire comparison before learner inquiry.
findings.acceptance: First-time learner understands why the bench matters, identifies the first action and can explain the meaning of each displayed measurement as it appears. Teacher reviews narrative continuity, cognitive scaffolding and emotional engagement, not just palette or technical completion. Do not implement until findings collection concludes.

findings.source: User screenshot M7-D2 and direct feedback, 2026-11-15
findings.observation: User finds the active experiment schematic, incomprehensible and unengaging. A lights up and displays input 100 J, useful light 20 J, heat 80 J and efficiency 20%, but the interface provides no contextual interpretation of the bars or quantities. The station remains a textual target, not a perceptibly functioning measurement instrument.
findings.proposal: Integrate a character-guided first experiment and progressive visual feedback: represent energy entering the virtual lamp and splitting into light and heat, explain the quantities in plain language before introducing joules and efficiency, show why equal light permits comparison, and link observations to a meaningful subsequent action. Preserve exact model values, comparable scales, accessible alternatives and scientific uncertainty; avoid decorative animation, forced quizzes or adding information density.
findings.acceptance: A first-time learner can explain what changes when a lamp is tested, what input/light/heat mean and why the result matters to the mission; visual feedback conveys the experiment even before reading formal numbers. Human walkthrough required. No implementation until editorial findings collection is complete.

findings.source: Two user screenshots M7-D2, 2026-11-15; one measurement and three measurements with C and input-only criterion selected
findings.observation: Partial notebook with A only shows numeric table, reset and disabled presentation without contextual next-step guidance. Completed notebook becomes a multiple-choice form detached from narrative. With C selected and input-only criterion selected, feedback compares C and A but does not explicitly explain why input alone is insufficient as a general efficiency criterion; equal useful light is the controlling condition. User has not explicitly commented on these screenshots; findings are advisory interpretation.
findings.proposal: Make notebook an incremental character-linked inquiry tool: contextual guidance to collect a second measurement; visual side-by-side comparison emphasizing same useful light, different input and heat; support learner explanation using observations and optional oral discussion, not a forced multiple-choice quiz. Explain that lower input is meaningful when useful output is held constant, and distinguish correct choice from incomplete reasoning. Retain accessible numeric table, exact model values, reset safeguards and voluntary revision.
findings.acceptance: With one measurement learner understands why another is needed; with multiple measurements learner can identify the invariant, compare quantities and justify the recommendation. Feedback distinguishes choice and reasoning and links conclusion to narrative task. Human review required; no implementation until findings collection concludes.
